findings: The 2026-11-07 capture identifies the Terminal SDK v6.0.0 migration guide and consists of a navigation index routing developers to separate iOS and Android variants. The pinned body supplies no platform-specific prerequisites, operational actors or SDK/payment state transitions.

The 2026-05-01 raw preserves the combined v5.0.0 guide for both platform variants, including before/after examples and historical behaviors. The existing v5.0.0 source and the versioned inbound Stripe Terminal concept and Stripe index routes correctly anchor that evidence.

Add a separately labeled 2026-11-07 v6.0.0 index pointer to the existing v5 source for same-URL retrieval, preserve the original v5 raw authority, and correct the v5 wording using the historical evidence. The v6 platform links are unread navigation.
substantive_changes: The version designation changes from 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 at the canonical route, a change in document scope. No new SDK runtime behavior can be established from the pinned v6 landing body.

The capture replaces the combined full-text body with an `Index` heading and platform-variant links. Those additions are presentation and navigation. Text shown removed in the stored diff signifies a changed capture representation.
historical_claims_to_preserve: v5 combines collect and confirm for payment, setup intents and refunds. Existing two-step payment methods still work, unified payment is recommended, and the two-step refund methods are deprecated.
Customer cancellation is enabled by default on supported readers, with iOS enum and Android DISABLE_IF_AVAILABLE opt-out. Preserve reconnect state and nil/null qualifications separately by SDK.

iOS v5 raises the minimum to iOS 15, while existing iOS 4.x still supports iOS 14+. Retain the pre-singleton token-provider initialization and use of discovery builders. Android init requires a nullable OfflineListener, and the Kotlin coroutine module is optional.

Interac refunds using a PaymentIntent ID require its clientSecret. The charge-ID path does not require it. Android Apps on Devices renames the Handoff classes and Maven artifact and Stripe says it will no longer update the old artifact.

Historical Android Tap to Pay requirements cover SDK 5.0.0+, Android 13+, hardware-backed key agreement, and the production-only discovery failure for enabled debug options with its simulated-reader exception. Discover acceptance is labeled public preview in the v5 overview.
conflicts: Source line 18 says processPaymentIntent replaces the two-step methods. The v5 iOS and Android guide says both existing payment methods continue to work and recommends the unified call (old raw lines 42-48 and old raw lines 445-451). Only the cited two-step refund methods are explicitly called deprecated (old raw line 89 and old raw line 504).

Source line 24 conflates a nil iOS reader during reconnect (old raw lines 255-257) with Android's documented null reader during initial connection, despite the Android section introducing the RECONNECTING enum and illustrating it separately (old raw lines 687-689 and old raw lines 712-724).

Source line 26 generalizes easyConnect without integration scope. iOS 5.1+ names smart readers and Tap to Pay, Android names smart readers, Tap to Pay and Apps on Devices, and the serial/ID filters are documented for Internet discovery (old raw lines 295-297, old raw lines 357-359, old raw lines 728-730 and old raw lines 776-778).

Source line 42 states the Android Tap to Pay debug-options error without the production discovery condition and simulated-reader exception. The older raw also distinguishes the Android 13 runtime minimum and hardware-backed key agreement check, with FEATURE_HARDWARE_KEYSTORE version 100+ as a check (old raw lines 938-946).
unresolved_questions: The assigned capture contains no iOS or Android v6.0.0 variant body, leaving behavior, prerequisites and state transitions for either v6 SDK unverified.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/references/sdk-migration-guide, the 2026-11-07 capture identifies v6.0.0 and routes app developers to separate iOS and Android variants (new raw lines 1-14). The complete landing body documents no v6 integration prerequisites, payment/reader state transitions or functional actor roles. The 2026-05-01 capture underlying source-stripe-terminal-sdk-migration-guide addresses developers upgrading iOS or Android from pre-v5 versions, documents single-call collect and confirm for payments, refunds and setup intents and customer cancellation on supported readers (old raw lines 12-32 and old raw lines 437-451), and covers iOS 15 minimum (old raw lines 34-38), the Android nullable OfflineListener in Terminal.init (old raw lines 663-667) and Android Tap to Pay device and production/simulated conditions (old raw lines 938-946). The summary describes that v5 material. It needs to clarify that the old payment methods still work (old raw lines 42-48 and old raw lines 445-451) and distinguish a nil connectedReader during iOS reconnect from the Android statement of null during initial connection, alongside the RECONNECTING enum (old raw lines 255-257 and old raw lines 687-689).
